import Init

-- Supplementary ordinary-Lean allocation control, not an upstream test edit.
-- A small child buffer supplies nonzero bytes without a large disk artifact.
def main (args : List String) : IO UInt32 := do
  let some text := args.head? | throw <| IO.userError "expected byte count"
  let some count := text.toNat? | throw <| IO.userError "invalid byte count"
  if count == 0 || count.toUSize.toNat != count then
    throw <| IO.userError "byte count does not fit this runtime"
  let child ← IO.Process.spawn {
    cmd := "python3"
    args := #["-c", "import sys\nn=int(sys.argv[1]); chunk=b'Z'*65536\nwhile n:\n k=min(n,len(chunk)); sys.stdout.buffer.write(chunk[:k]); n-=k\nsys.stdout.buffer.flush()", toString count]
    stdin := .null
    stdout := .piped
    stderr := .inherit }
  let bytes ← child.stdout.read count.toUSize
  let status ← child.wait
  if status != 0 || bytes.size != count then
    throw <| IO.userError s!"read mismatch: status={status}, requested={count}, actual={bytes.size}"
  for index in [0, count / 2, count - 1] do
    if bytes[index]! != 90 then
      throw <| IO.userError s!"unexpected byte at {index}"
  IO.println s!"read {bytes.size} bytes with value 90"
  return 0
limitations: The baseline size increase stopped at 64 MiB after the Deno peak reached 5.23 GiB. No baseline 256 MiB or multi-GiB read was attempted, and guard limits were not raised.
Read comparisons validate exact lengths and first/middle/final nonzero bytes with successful writer shutdown, not every byte or all filesystem edge cases.
Response buffers still clone across the port and copy through the C++ Reply vector into Lean data. Larger payloads, short-read backing-buffer costs, and further copy reduction remain open.
Timing and peak comparisons are individual local measurements, not statistical performance guarantees.

Native-memory64 Bun uses the opt-in local 8 GiB build; the separate lowered controls use released Bun. Full suites, packaged full-runtime integration, and other operating systems/architectures remain unfinished.
